sources.note: Main homepage. Describes two product lines (Enterprise and Office), Closed Loop patient journey, AI features (Ambient Assist, Intelligent Agent), 26 specialty templates, AWS cloud hosting, mobile EHR, and notable customer logos.

ONC mandatory disclosures page. Lists Enterprise 8 certification (HTI-1 Phase 2), older Ambulatory EHR versions, Mirth Connect versions, and QSIDental. Discloses additional costs for patient portal, external connectivity (lab/registry interfaces), Bulk C-CDA Export Utility, and Healthwise patient education.

Enterprise EHR product page. Describes partnership model, interoperability, specialty-specific content, patient engagement, streamlined charting, value-based care. Lists PM features: scheduling, eligibility, billing, claims, reporting, analytics. Notes Enterprise 8 HTI-1 Phase 2 certification.

Practice Management product page. Details scheduling, automated claim scrubbing, Background Business Processor, cost estimator, automated charge review, coding compliance, billing, collections, financial analytics, clearinghouse/EDI. Black Book #1 PM ranking for 9 consecutive years.
Specialties landing page. Confirms two product lines (Enterprise for mid-size+, Office for small). Lists specialty-specific content availability. Limited detail on specific specialties on this page.

Referenced in web search results. Describes FQHC/CHC support with integrated medical, behavioral health, dental, and human services in a single EHR. Supports UDS+, CMS, PQRS reporting. Whole-person care delivery.

2022 press release about NextGen's Behavioral Health Suite. Covers outpatient mental health, substance use disorder, crisis intervention, residential treatment, I/DD services, autism documentation, and home/community-based services.
Thoma Bravo acquisition press release (Nov 2023). $1.8B deal, $23.95/share. States NextGen serves 100,000+ providers managing 65M+ patients. Company taken private, delisted from Nasdaq.
G2 reviews. Users praise customization, workflow efficiency. Complain about click-heavy navigation, outdated UI, and learning curve.
Capterra reviews of NextGen Enterprise. Users highlight customizable templates, strong billing features. Complaints about complexity, mixed support quality, and older-looking interface.
Forbes Advisor review. Notes comprehensive feature set, no free trial or public pricing, steep learning curve for complex deployments.
Healthcare IT News coverage of Thoma Bravo acquisition. Provides company history context — founded 1973 as QSI, went public 1982, NextGen subsidiary acquired 2001.
Enlyft market data. Reports 2,400+ organizations using NextGen Healthcare, primarily US-based healthcare and hospital sectors.
